plugin.name: Runbooks
plugin.description: Runbooks an agent proposes and a person runs, one approved command at a time, with every output kept.

use.title: Use Runbooks
use.description: Read runbooks and run their steps on hosts you can connect to.

manageTokens.title: Manage Runbooks tokens
manageTokens.description: Make and revoke the tokens agents use to propose runbooks.

list.emptyHint: An agent with a Runbooks token proposes them; they show up here.

step.notesPlaceholder: Notes for this step. Saved when you leave the box; agents can read them.

run.ok: The command finished with exit code 0.
run.notOk: The command failed. See the output.
run.byTerminal: Sent to a terminal by {{user}} at {{time}}
run.pastePlaceholder: Paste the terminal output here, then mark the step done or failed.

repeat.titleStep: This step already ran. Run it again?
repeat.titleHash: This command ran on this host in the last 24 hours. Run it again?

order.hint: Not done yet: {{steps}}. Run this step anyway?

terminal.noneHint: Open a terminal to this host. When it is connected, press Send to terminal again.
terminal.opened: Terminal opened. Press Send to terminal again once it is connected.
terminal.noHost: This host is not available to you.
terminal.confirmHint: The command is typed into the terminal but not run: you press Enter there. Then paste the output back here.

terminal.sendFailed: Could not send to the terminal. Copy the command instead.

tokens.title: Agent tokens
tokens.intro: An agent uses a token to propose runbooks and read their results. A token can never run a command. It may name only the hosts you tick for it, and it sees the runbooks made with your tokens.
tokens.namePlaceholder: Token name, like the agent's name
tokens.once: Token for {{name}}. Copy it now: it is not shown again.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.revokeHint: Agents using it are refused from now on.
tokens.pickHosts: Tick at least one host the token may use.
tokens.noHosts: You have no hosts to give a token.

error.stale: The step changed since you saw it. Check the new command before you run it.
